To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the electrodisinfection of urban wastewater with Al electrodes is possible, and that the performance of this process is strongly dependent on the initial effluent characteristics and the cell configuration.
the use of a bipolar aluminum electrode allows the simultaneous electrocoagulation and electrodisinfection of urban wastewaters.

the proposed integrated ED-EC process with aluminum bipolar electrode is able to achieve a complete disinfection and a turbidity removal higher than 90% of urban wastewaters at an applied charge of 0 A h dm(-2) when using BDD anodes, and a current density of about 11 A m(-2) when DSA anodes are used.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new electrochemical cell for urban wastewater treatment, where the electrocoagulation and the electrodisinfection processes can be carried out at the same time.
the optimization of a new electrochemical cell, with a bipolar electrode made of aluminum, for wastewater treatment.
the optimization of a new electrochemical process for the treatment of urban wastewater, which allows to obtain an effluent with a high quality.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the integrated ED-EC process is a feasible and effective process for wastewater reclamation.
the use of the proposed electrochemical system for urban wastewater reutilization is possible.
the use of the integrated ED-EC process with BDD and DSA anodes allows to obtain treated effluents with low levels of E. coli and turbidity, which can be reused in different applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it is possible, using this novel electrochemical cell, to achieve a 98% of removal of E. Coli and a 100% turbidity removal from urban wastewater.

the electrodisinfection process can be carried out in a bipolar cell, where the electrocoagulation process is simultaneously carried out, with the use of aluminum bipolar electrodes, and that the use of BDD as anode is more efficient in removing E. coli from the wastewater than the use of DSA as anode.
the use of bipolar electrodes in electrochemical cells allows us to carry out, in the same reactor, two different processes, electrodisinfection and electrocoagulaton.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible the simultaneous electrodisinfection and electrocoagulaton of urban wastewaters using aluminum bipolar electrodes.
this integrated electrodisinfective-electrocoagulation system could be a promising technology for the regeneration of urban wastewater.

it is possible, using an electrochemical cell with bipolar aluminum electrodes, to remove simultaneously the E. coli and the turbidity from actual urban wastewater, obtaining a treated effluent suitable for irrigation purposes.
